questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Non-Aligned Movement (NAM):
1. Its first summit was held at Belgrade in 1961.
2. It has a permanent secretariat headquartered in New Delhi.
3. Josip Broz Tito, Gamal Abdel Nasser and Jawaharlal Nehru were among its founding leaders.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: NAM was founded at Belgrade in 1961 by Nehru, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno and Nkrumah. It deliberately has no formal charter or permanent secretariat; coordination is through the rotating Chair, so statement 2 is wrong.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 1; MEA
questions.h: Five founders: N-N-T-S-N = Nehru, Nasser, Tito, Sukarno, Nkrumah.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: India's policy of non-alignment meant that India remained neutral and indifferent to disputes between other countries.
Statement-II: India's non-alignment involved taking independent positions on international issues on their merits, while actively opposing colonialism and racial discrimination.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Non-alignment was not neutrality or isolation: Nehru's India mediated in Korea and Indo-China and led the anti-colonial campaign. Statement-I confuses non-alignment with neutrality, while Statement-II correctly describes it.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 1

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in chronological order (earliest first):
A. Algiers summit of NAM
B. Bandung Conference
C. New Delhi summit of NAM
D. Belgrade summit of NAM
questions.e: Bandung (1955) preceded the first NAM summit at Belgrade (1961). The fourth summit was at Algiers (1973) and the seventh at New Delhi (1983), where Indira Gandhi took over as Chair.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 1

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Commonwealth:
1. The Commonwealth Secretariat is located at Marlborough House, London.
2. The office of Head of the Commonwealth passes automatically to the British monarch by heredity.
3. Membership is open only to countries that were once British colonies.
4. India continued as a member after becoming a republic in 1950 because of the London Declaration of 1949.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The Secretariat sits at Marlborough House, and the London Declaration of 1949 let republics remain members by accepting the monarch as a symbolic Head. The Headship is not hereditary (leaders chose Charles in 2018), and Rwanda and Mozambique show that membership is not restricted to ex-British colonies.

questions.q: Which one of the following countries left the Commonwealth in 1961 and was readmitted in 1994?
questions.e: South Africa withdrew in 1961 when it became a republic amid criticism of apartheid, and rejoined in 1994 after the first non-racial elections. Pakistan left in 1972 and returned in 1989, Zimbabwe left in 2003 and has not returned, and Ireland left in 1949.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC):
1. It was founded in 1969 after the arson attack at the Al-Aqsa Mosque in Jerusalem.
2. Its headquarters is located in Jeddah.
3. India is an observer state of the OIC.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The OIC emerged from the Rabat summit of 1969 held in response to the Al-Aqsa arson, and it is headquartered in Jeddah. India is not an observer; observers include Russia and Thailand, and India has only been invited as a guest.

questions.q: In March 2019, India's External Affairs Minister addressed the OIC Council of Foreign Ministers as Guest of Honour. The meeting was held in:
questions.e: The 46th OIC Council of Foreign Ministers met in Abu Dhabi on 1-2 March 2019, and India attended as Guest of Honour on UAE's invitation. Islamabad hosted a later session (2022), which is why it is tempting.

questions.q: The first Islamic Summit that led to the creation of the Organisation of the Islamic Conference (later renamed Organisation of Islamic Cooperation in 2011) was held in 1969 at:
questions.e: The 1969 Rabat summit, called after the Al-Aqsa arson, created the OIC. Lahore hosted the second summit (1974) and Jeddah became the headquarters.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the G7:
1. Canada was among the participants in the first summit at Rambouillet in 1975.
2. Russia was suspended from the then G8 in 2014 after the annexation of Crimea.
3. It has no permanent secretariat, and the presidency rotates among members every year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1975 Rambouillet meeting had six participants and Canada joined only in 1976. Russia was suspended in 2014 and the grouping reverted to the G7, which works through a rotating presidency without a secretariat.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions); Reuters, 2014
questions.h: Six at start (G6, 1975), Canada made it seven in 1976.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the G20:
1. It was formed in 1999 after the Asian financial crisis as a forum of finance ministers and central bank governors.
2. Its first Leaders' Summit was held in Washington DC in 2008.
3. It has a permanent secretariat in Geneva.
4. The African Union was admitted as a permanent member at the New Delhi Summit in 2023.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The G20 began in 1999 and moved to leaders' level in 2008 after the global financial crisis. It has no permanent secretariat (a Troika and rotating presidency run it), and the AU joined as a permanent member at New Delhi in September 2023.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The theme of India's G20 Presidency in 2023 was 'One Earth, One Family, One Future'.
Statement-II: The theme was derived from the Sanskrit phrase 'Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam'.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The 2023 theme is the English rendering of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam, the idea that the world is one family. So Statement-II explains Statement-I.

questions.q: The 2025 G20 Leaders' Summit, the first G20 summit held on the African continent, took place in:
questions.e: South Africa held the 2025 presidency after Brazil (Rio de Janeiro, 2024), and the leaders met in Johannesburg in November 2025. Nairobi is tempting because it is not a G20 country at all.

questions.q:
Match the founding leaders of the Non-Aligned Movement with their countries.
Leader: A. Josip Broz Tito  B. Gamal Abdel Nasser  C. Kwame Nkrumah  D. Sukarno
Country: 1. Ghana  2. Yugoslavia  3. Indonesia  4. Egypt
questions.e: Tito led Yugoslavia, Nasser Egypt, Nkrumah Ghana and Sukarno Indonesia; with Nehru they are called the five founders of NAM. The wrong options swap the two North African and Southeast Asian leaders.
questions.s: NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics Ch 1

questions.q: Which one of the following was admitted to the Commonwealth in 1995 despite having never been a British colony?
questions.e: Mozambique, a former Portuguese colony and surrounded by Commonwealth states, joined in 1995 and Rwanda (Belgian-ruled) in 2009. Ghana, Zambia and Sri Lanka were British territories and members from independence.

questions.q: The Group of 77 (G77) was established in 1964 on the occasion of the:
o: first session of UNCTAD at Geneva
questions.e: Seventy-seven developing countries issued a joint declaration at the end of the first UNCTAD session in 1964, to promote their collective economic interests. It is a UN-based coalition, unlike NAM, which is a summit-level political movement.
questions.s: un.org (G77 history); Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy

questions.q: The 2024 Commonwealth Heads of Government Meeting (CHOGM) was hosted by:
questions.e: CHOGM 2024 was held in Apia, Samoa, in October 2024. Rwanda hosted the 2022 meeting, Malta the 2015 meeting and Sri Lanka the 2013 meeting.

questions.q: Which one of the following is a member of the G20 but not of the G7?
questions.e: Argentina is a G20 member. Italy, Canada and Japan belong to both the G7 and the G20.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Panchsheel:
1. The five principles were formally enunciated in the 1954 agreement between India and China relating to Tibet.
2. The five principles were first adopted at the Bandung Conference in 1955.
3. They include mutual non-aggression and peaceful co-existence.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Panchsheel was incorporated in the 1954 Agreement on Trade and Intercourse between India and the Tibet Region of China, a year before Bandung, where they were carried into the ten principles of the Bandung Declaration.
questions.s: Bipan Chandra, India Since Independence; NCERT Class 12, Contemporary World Politics

questions.q: The Statute of Westminster (1931), relevant to the evolution of the Commonwealth, was passed to:
o: extend British parliamentary supremacy over the Dominions
give legal effect to the equality of status of the Dominions defined at the 1926 Imperial Conference
create the Commonwealth Secretariat in London
questions.e: The 1926 Balfour formula called Britain and the Dominions autonomous and equal in status, and the 1931 Statute enacted this into law. It ended the British Parliament's power to legislate for Dominions without their consent, so it is the opposite of extending supremacy.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the G20?
questions.e: The G20 has 19 countries plus the European Union and the African Union, and South Africa is the only African country among them. Nigeria is a large African economy but not a member.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bretton Woods Conference:
1. It was held in July 1944 at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire.
2. The system it created pegged currencies to the US dollar, which was convertible into gold.
3. It established the World Trade Organization.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 1944 conference created the IMF and IBRD and a dollar-gold exchange standard with adjustable pegs. The WTO came only in 1995 after the Uruguay Round, as the failed International Trade Organization of the 1940s was never created.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions)
questions.h: Bretton Woods = twins (IMF, World Bank); trade was left orphaned until GATT.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Monetary Fund (IMF):
1. It is headquartered in New York.
2. It provides long-term concessional loans mainly for development projects.
3. By convention, its Managing Director has been a European.
4. Every member has an equal number of votes irrespective of its quota.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The IMF sits in Washington DC and mainly lends against balance of payments problems, while long-term development loans come from the World Bank. Votes depend on quotas (plus basic votes), and by an old understanding the IMF head is European and the World Bank head American.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh, Indian Economy (International Economic Institutions); imf.org

questions.q:
Match the World Bank Group institutions with their functions.
Institution: A. IBRD  B. IDA  C. IFC  D. MIGA
Function: 1. Concessional loans and grants to the poorest countries  2. Investment in the private sector of developing countries  3. Guarantees against political risk for foreign investors  4. Loans to middle-income and creditworthy low-income countries
questions.e: IBRD lends to middle-income countries, IDA gives soft credit to the poorest, IFC works with private firms and MIGA gives political-risk guarantees. The wrong options mix IFC (investment) with MIGA (insurance).
questions.h: I-B-R-D = Bigger loans; I-D-A = Aid for poorest; IFC = Firms; MIGA = Guarantees.

questions.q:
Which of the following reports are published by the World Bank?
1. Global Financial Stability Report
2. World Development Report
3. Logistics Performance Index
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The World Development Report and the Logistics Performance Index are World Bank products. The Global Financial Stability Report is published by the IMF.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The World Bank discontinued its 'Doing Business' report in 2021.
Statement-II: The decision followed a review that found data irregularities in earlier editions of the report.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The Bank stopped the report in September 2021 after an audit found irregularities in data of the 2018 and 2020 editions. So the irregularities explain the discontinuation.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the World Trade Organization (WTO):
1. It came into being on 1 January 1995 after the Uruguay Round.
2. It replaced GATT 1947 by discarding GATT rules entirely.
3. Its Ministerial Conference meets at least once every two years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The WTO was created under the Marrakesh Agreement of 1994 and took effect in 1995. GATT 1947 rules were not discarded; they were folded into GATT 1994, which sits within the WTO framework.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: The WTO Appellate Body has been unable to hear appeals since December 2019.
Statement-II: The United States has blocked the consensus needed to appoint new Appellate Body members, leaving it without the minimum number of members.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Appointments to the Appellate Body need consensus in the Dispute Settlement Body, and the US has blocked them since 2017. Hearing a case needs three members, so by December 2019 the body had lost its quorum.

questions.q: Who became the first woman and the first African to serve as Director-General of the WTO?
questions.e: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala of Nigeria took office in March 2021. Azevedo (Brazil) was her predecessor, while Lagarde and Georgieva headed the IMF.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about WTO Ministerial Conferences:
1. The Trade Facilitation Agreement was concluded at Bali in 2013.
2. At Nairobi in 2015, members decided to eliminate agricultural export subsidies.
3. The twelfth Ministerial Conference was held in Buenos Aires.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Bali (MC9, 2013) gave the TFA and Nairobi (MC10, 2015) the export subsidy decision. MC11 was at Buenos Aires in 2017, and MC12 in 2022 was held at Geneva.
questions.h: Hook: Bali = Facilitation; Nairobi = No export subsidies.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about subsidies under the WTO Agreement on Agriculture:
1. Green box subsidies, such as research and extension services, are exempt from reduction commitments.
2. Amber box measures, such as administered price support, are subject to reduction commitments.
3. Blue box payments are linked to production-limiting programmes.
4. Decoupled direct income support to farmers is classified under the Amber box.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: Green box measures cause minimal trade distortion, Amber box measures are trade-distorting and capped, and Blue box payments come with production limits. Decoupled income support is a Green box measure, not Amber.
questions.h: Traffic lights: Green = go, Amber = slow down, Blue = limited.

questions.q: Which one of the following WTO agreements deals with product standards and technical regulations that may create obstacles to trade?
o: Agreement on Sanitary and Phytosanitary Measures
Agreement on Technical Barriers to Trade
General Agreement on Trade in Services
questions.e: The TBT Agreement covers technical regulations and standards for products. The SPS Agreement covers food safety and animal and plant health measures, TRIMS covers investment measures and GATS covers services.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the principles of the WTO system:
1. Under the Most Favoured Nation principle, a trade advantage given to one member must be extended to all members.
2. Regional trade agreements such as customs unions and free trade areas are permitted as exceptions to the MFN rule, subject to conditions.
3. National treatment requires imported goods, once they have cleared customs, to be treated no less favourably than domestic goods.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: MFN rules out discrimination among trading partners, while national treatment rules out discrimination against imports once inside the border. GATT Article XXIV allows customs unions and free trade areas as an exception.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB):
1. It is headquartered in Beijing.
2. It began operations in January 2016.
3. India is the largest shareholder of the bank.
4. The United States and Japan are among its largest shareholders.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: The AIIB is based in Beijing and opened for business in January 2016. China is the largest shareholder and India the second; the US and Japan have stayed outside the bank.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the New Development Bank (NDB) is NOT correct?
o: Its first President was from Brazil.
The agreement to establish it was signed at the 2014 BRICS Summit at Fortaleza.
Its initial authorised capital was US$ 100 billion.
questions.e: The NDB's first President was K. V. Kamath of India, who came in on a rotating arrangement among founding members. The other statements are correct: it is based in Shanghai, was agreed at Fortaleza in 2014 and had $100 billion authorised capital.

questions.q: The BRICS Contingent Reserve Arrangement (CRA) is meant to:
o: finance infrastructure and sustainable development projects in member countries
settle intra-BRICS trade in a common digital currency
supervise cross-border banking operations of member countries
provide liquidity support to members facing short-term balance of payments pressures
questions.e: The CRA is a $100 billion pooled-reserve framework to help members tackle short-term BoP stress, a BRICS-version of an IMF safety net. Project finance is the job of the New Development Bank, not the CRA.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Bank for International Settlements (BIS):
1. It was established in 1944 at Bretton Woods along with the IMF.
2. It is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.
3. Its shareholders are central banks.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The BIS dates from 1930 and is the oldest international financial organisation; it was set up to handle German reparations. It is based in Basel, owned by central banks and often called the central banks' bank.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT one of the three pillars of Basel II norms?
questions.e: Basel II (2004) rested on minimum capital, supervisory review and market discipline. The Liquidity Coverage Ratio was introduced later under Basel III after the 2007-09 financial crisis.

questions.q: Under Basel III, the capital conservation buffer to be maintained over and above the minimum capital requirement is:
questions.e: Basel III requires a buffer of 2.5 per cent of RWA, held in common equity, to absorb losses in stress. The 4.5 per cent figure is the minimum Common Equity Tier 1 ratio.
questions.s: bis.org; RBI Master Circular on Basel III

questions.q: The Financial Stability Board, set up by the G20 in 2009, has its secretariat hosted by:
o: the Bank for International Settlements at Basel
the International Monetary Fund at Washington DC
the World Bank at Washington DC
questions.e: The FSB succeeded the Financial Stability Forum and coordinates global financial regulation for the G20. Its secretariat is hosted by the BIS in Basel, the same city as the Basel Committee.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Financial Action Task Force (FATF):
1. It was established in 1989 at the G7 Summit in Paris.
2. Its secretariat is housed at the OECD headquarters in Paris.
3. India became a FATF member in 2010.
4. Its standards are known as the FATF Recommendations, of which there are forty.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.e: FATF is an inter-governmental body, not a UN body, born at the 1989 Paris G7 summit and housed at the OECD. India joined in 2010, and its 40 Recommendations are the global standard against money laundering and terror financing.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
Statement-I: Placing a country on the FATF 'grey list' automatically imposes United Nations sanctions on it.
Statement-II: Grey-listed jurisdictions are those under increased monitoring that have committed to resolve identified strategic deficiencies in a set time.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The grey list signals closer scrutiny and can raise borrowing costs and deter investors, but it is not a sanction regime. The 'call for action' (black list) is the harsher category.

questions.q: Pakistan was placed on the FATF grey list in June 2018. It was removed from the list in:
questions.e: FATF removed Pakistan from increased monitoring in October 2022 after it completed its action plans. It stayed through 2020 and 2021, when the plenaries kept it on the list.

questions.q:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their establishment (earliest first):
A. WTO
B. Bank for International Settlements
C. AIIB (start of operations)
D. FATF
questions.e: BIS was founded in 1930, the FATF in 1989, the WTO in 1995 and the AIIB began operations in 2016.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of institutions and their headquarters:
1. Bank for International Settlements : Zurich
2. AIIB : Beijing
3. Asian Development Bank : Manila
4. New Development Bank : Mumbai
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched?
questions.e: The BIS is in Basel, not Zurich, and the NDB is in Shanghai, not Mumbai. AIIB (Beijing) and ADB (Manila) are correct.

questions.q: Which one of the following was a founding member of OPEC when it was formed in Baghdad in 1960?
questions.e: The five founders were Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Saudi Arabia and Venezuela. Libya joined in 1962, the UAE (Abu Dhabi) in 1967 and Nigeria in 1971.

questions.q: Which one of the following reports is published by UNCTAD?
questions.e: UNCTAD, based in Geneva since 1964, publishes the World Investment Report on FDI flows. Global Economic Prospects is a World Bank report, GFSR an IMF report and Global Risks Report a World Economic Forum one.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a member of the OECD?
questions.e: The OECD, headquartered in Paris, has Mexico (1994), Chile (2010) and Turkey (1961) as members. India works with it as a key partner but is not a member.

questions.q: Which IMF lending facility is reserved for members with very strong economic fundamentals and policy track records and provides large precautionary access?
questions.e: The Flexible Credit Line is a precautionary facility for pre-qualified countries with strong fundamentals. The EFF and SBA are programme-based loans with conditions, and PRGT is concessional lending to low-income countries.

questions.q: In October 2016, which currency joined the US dollar, euro, yen and pound sterling in the IMF's Special Drawing Rights (SDR) basket?
questions.e: The renminbi became the fifth SDR currency on 1 October 2016 after the IMF found it freely usable. The SDR is a reserve asset created in 1969, not a currency.
questions.h: SDR = Dollar, Euro, Yen, Pound, Yuan.

questions.q: The Doha Development Round of multilateral trade negotiations was launched at the WTO Ministerial Conference held in:
questions.e: The Doha Round was launched in November 2001 at Doha, Qatar, with development concerns at its centre. It has remained largely stalled, and the Bali package of 2013 was a partial outcome.
